subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Novamed API offboard planning
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Kline <sasha.k@novamed.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@novamed.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Novamed API offboard planning

Hi Sasha / Tom,

Thanks for your time today — appreciated the candid walkthrough of Novamed's current stack and constraints. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, success criteria you described, and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please call out anything I missed or mischaracterized.

Summary of pain points (what you emphasized)
- Cost volatility on current OpenAI / Anthropic usage: peak burst billing on inference-heavy workflows (chiefly batch clinical summarization).
- Latency spikes during heavy inference and async batch overlap — impacts analyst throughput for same-day reports.
- Data isolation & compliance: need for VPC + KMS-managed keys and stricter audit logs.
- Feature gap between proprietary API features (tooling, multi-turn state) and open-model parity — concerned about function-calling and streaming parity.

Current footprint we captured
- Production: OpenAI (gpt-4o for chat + embeddings), Anthropic for a smaller assistant path.
- Monthly token volume: ~12M tokens (peaks to ~30M during monthly analytics jobs).
- Critical workloads:
  * Clinical summarization pipeline (batch, high context, ~8k average prompt + KV cache reuse)
  * Patient-facing triage assistant (sub-second response targets)
  * Vector search/embedding index for clinical retrieval (512-d embeddings today)
- Security: Customer-managed KMS in AWS in progress; currently using vendor-encrypted keys for embeddings storage.

Compatibility & must-haves for an open-model offboard
- Streaming + chunked responses (for UI latency masking)
- Function/tool calling or structured JSON output support (diagnostic codes, triage actions)
- Embedding dimensional parity or mapping strategy (current pipelines expect 512 dims)
- Tokenizer determinism for existing prompts (avoid large prompt drift)
- Context window >= 32k for summarization jobs (or a plan to chunk + stitch)

Model shortlist (initial candidates we discussed)
- Llama 3 family (13B / 70B) — good instruction-following; we discussed quantized variants for cost/perf.
- Mistral Instruct / Large variants — promising for instruction tuning, good throughput on GPU.
- Open-weights 30B-class candidate (community variants) — potential cost sweet spot for batch jobs.

Success criteria (how you'll evaluate PoC)
- Quality: automatic eval pass rate on your prompt suite within 5% of current vendor baseline (pairwise evals).
- Latency: P99 for patient triage endpoint <= 700ms (target), or no more than 20% regression.
- Cost: target >= 30% unit-cost reduction for batch summarization relative to current blended rate.
- Security: VPC + KMS and audit log delivery to your SIEM during pilot.

Proposed next steps & timeline
1) Technical kickoff & infra checklist (this week): confirm VPC/KMS readiness, sample prompts & dataset for eval (we need ~200 representative prompts per workload).
2) Compatibility matrix from Redwood (attached): mapping for streaming, embeddings dims, tokenizer notes.
3) Short PoC (4–6 weeks): pilot Llama3-13B quantized + Mistral-instruct on dedicated pool; run eval suite, measure cost/latency.
4) Commercial check-in: SOW draft and preliminary pricing — we attached a SOW draft for your review.

Deliverables well send by EOD tomorrow
- Compatibility matrix (xlsx) — mapping of features and blockers
- Short SOW draft (pdf) — initial pricing and pilot scope

If that looks right, can you:
- Share the sample prompt set + one example full clinical document (deidentified) for the summarization workload?
- Confirm whether the triage endpoint requires strict sub-second SLAs globally or just in us-east-1?

Thanks again — Ill book the technical kickoff for Thursday if that works for your engineering lead.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri@redwood.com

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 3:10 PM Priyom Das <pri@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for your time today — appreciated the candid walkthrough of Novamed's current stack and constraints. Below is a concise recap ...

Thanks Priyom — this is a good summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The 32k context need is for the nightly summarization job specifically; the triage assistant is typically under 8k.
- Embedding dimension today is 512 but were open to a mapping layer if the target model uses a different vector size.
- For the SLA question: currently only US East (primary) needs the sub-second promise; for other regions we can accept slightly higher P99s.

We will share a de-identified clinical doc and 250 sample prompts by tomorrow afternoon. Can you include an explicit checklist for KMS requirements (policies we need to set on our side)?

Also: wed like to see a quick cost estimate for the two shortlisted options (Llama3-13B quantized vs Mistral-instruct medium) for the monthly batch job — ballpark is fine.

Appreciate it — Sasha
